newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians stone PLO riot police.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians stone PLO riot police.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinian demonstrators stoned PLO police who tried to prevent them from reaching an Israeli position near the West Bank Ramallah self-rule enclave on Friday, witnesses said.
The Ramallah incident was the first time in the last three days of fierce clashes in the West Bank, Gaza and Arab East Jerusalem that the Palestinian Authority deployed riot police.

In some areas of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, such as Bethlehem, regular Palestinian police also tried to keep protesters from attacking Israeli positions. But in others, like Jericho and Tulkarm, police fired on Israeli soldiers as they had on the previous two days of pitched battles.
Seven Palestinians died in clashes on Friday -- three of them shot dead by Israeli forces on Jerusalem's Temple Mount. Two Israeli border policeman died in a gunbattle with Palestinians near Tulkarm.
Witnesses in Ramallah said some 40 riot police wearing navy blue uniforms and helmets and armed with clubs and shields came between Palestinian demonstrators and Israeli forces at a roadblock.

Israeli soldiers fired live and rubber-coated metal bullets at the demonstrators, wounding many of them. The riot police failed to turn back the demonstrators who after two hours of fighting dispersed on their own.

"Riot police pushed and shoved demonstrators in a failed attempt to turn them away from Israeli gunfire. Protesters stopped throwing stones at Israelis and began pelting the anti-riot police with stones," a witness said.
A senior police officer said: "We are doing this to protect them from Israeli bullets."
PLO security officials said on Friday that Palestinian President Yasser Arafat ordered his paramilitary troops to prevent friction between civilians and the Israeli army.

Moslem Friday prayers and Palestinian protest marches were the backdrop for the latest bloodshed. The week's unrest was touched off by Israel's opening of a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem under cover of darkness on Tuesday before dawn.
Sixty-six people -- 53 Palestinians and 13 Israeli soldiers -- have died in three days of clashes, Palestinian medical officials and Israeli security sources said on Friday.
